Subject: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback for MedNova (prod)

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this. MedNova has a new EU production deployment (PHI-adjacent) and our security/compliance team is insisting that all inference for that environment must: 

- run only on models hosted in the EU region,
- never fall back to a non-EU model or a reduced-variant model (no-fallback), and
- be pinned to a specific tested model family (we've proposed the redwood-3b-eu-quantized variant).

They've flagged two non-negotiables: geographic isolation and an absolute prohibition on fallback under any capacity pressure. Attached is our compliance brief for context.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is something you can commit to for production? If yes, MedNova will need:
- a written statement of the constraint,
- update to the DPA/SOW for the EU-only clause, and
- cost estimate for dedicated EU capacity.

Happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Cloud Engineering, MedNova Health

Thanks for the forward. Quick take + clarifying Qs: 

Summary of constraints (as I understand them):
- Regional isolation: routing to eu-* only.
- No fallback: under no circumstances should traffic be routed to any non-EU model/variant.
- Pin to redwood-3b-eu-quantized (customer-selected).

Questions / items to confirm:
1) Is MedNova expecting the model to be immutable (no patch/rollout) or can we do controlled maintenance windows?
2) Can they tolerate increased tail latency during peak times if we avoid fallback, or do they need strict P95 latency guarantees?

Implementation notes / tradeoffs:
- We can pin and hard-tether requests at the policy layer to an EU-only variant; that part is straightforward.
- No-fallback removes our main resilience path: when capacity is exhausted we currently shift to a smaller variant or a compatible regional replica. If we remove fallback we must either: 
  * provide guaranteed reserved capacity (Dedicated pool) sized for peak, or
  * accept dropped requests during saturation (not acceptable for most customers).
- Consequence: much higher committed cost for Dedicated capacity. Also complicates canary/rollout mechanics — we'd need a plan to perform model upgrades without violating the pinned contract.

Proposed next steps: 
- Priyom: rough capacity/cost estimate for a 99th percentile peak and steady state.
- Vanessa / Legal: confirm whether we can include a clause that allows emergency, mutually agreed maintenance fallbacks (e.g., signed SLA exception).

I'll sketch the product constraints for SRE/ops if you want.

-Marcus
Product Lead, Model Serving

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback for MedNova (prod)

Short ops assessment:

Feasibility: YES, with Dedicated EU pool. Implementation steps:
- Provision dedicated nodes in eu-west-1 attached to MedNova tenant (KVM/GKE + GPU nodes).
- Configure routing policy: strict region match + model variant pin. Disable automatic fallback policies for the route.
- Add capacity buffer: recommend 30% headroom above expected peak for safety.

Sizing / cost (ballpark):
- Baseline steady-state: 8x A100 40GB equiv (estimate).
- Peak buffer for 99th pct: +30% => 11 machines.
- Monthly committed cost estimate (incl infra, license, monitoring): ~€125k/month (very rough). Exact depends on sequence length distribution and request concurrency.

Operational risks:
- No-fallback means any spike beyond committed capacity could cause throttling/dropped requests rather than degraded model degrade. That may surface as outages to the customer.
- Autoscaling will need to be converted to manual/reserved or to use burst capacity that still respects the EU-only rule (we can do burst but it's expensive).

Alternatives to absolute no-fallback:
1) Soft tether: allow fallback only after an explicit, signed emergency escalation from MedNova (human-in-the-loop).
2) Canary tether: allow short-term fallback for <5 minutes for emergency maintenance with prior notice.

Attachments: I put a quick cost worksheet together.
[Attachment: cost_estimate_eu_dedicated.xlsx]

-- Priyom
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Dedicated

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback for MedNova (prod)

Legal note:
- We can agree to a regional-only deployment and a pinned model in the SOW, but we should not contractually promise "no-fallback under all circumstances" without a compensating clause. The risk: if we cannot serve due to a catastrophic hardware fault we become strictly liable for every outage.

Suggested contract language:
- Redwood will operate a dedicated EU-only serving pool for the customer and will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid fallback to non-EU variants.
- For emergency maintenance or catastrophic infrastructure events, Redwood may invoke an "Emergency Exception" only after written notice to the customer and with documented mitigation steps.
- Include SLA credits and an optional extended SLA (higher fee) that covers guaranteed reserved capacity.

Also: we need MedNova to sign a SOC2 addendum + updated DPA. Sales should own the signature path.

I'll draft the SOW/contract clause this afternoon.

-Lauren
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
